mainTopic: The dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a thought from one עבודה to another, and רב ששת's challenge from רבי יוסי's קל וחומר.
overview: The גמרא first finishes explaining the three opinions in the משנה about slaughtering for a gentile. The תנא קמא does not learn ordinary slaughter (חוץ) from קדשים (פנים). רבי אליעזר does learn it. רבי יוסי holds that even with קדשים, one person's thought cannot ruin another person's act. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about someone who slaughters an animal planning to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for עבודה זרה. רבי יוחנן forbids it, because a thought about a later עבודה counts and we learn חוץ מפנים, while ריש לקיש permits it. They argue the same way about a קרבן slaughtered לשמה with a plan to sprinkle its blood שלא לשמה. The גמרא explains why both arguments had to be recorded. Then רב ששת challenges them from רבי יוסי's קל וחומר in the משנה. He shows how one half of it hurts ריש לקיש and the other half hurts רבי יוחנן. Finally רב ששת answers his own challenge: רבי יוסי was talking about a wrong thought during the ארבע עבודות. The rewording of רבי יוסי's קל וחומר continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Finishing the תנא קמא and explaining רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its line that the תנא קמא does not learn outside from inside. It then explains that רבי אליעזר does learn outside from inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The תנא קמא holds that] we do not learn [outside from inside]. And רבי אליעזר comes to say: we do learn outside from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of explaining the opinions in the משנה about slaughtering for a gentile. Here it finishes the תנא קמא's view and explains רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether rules about bad intent in קדשים (inside the מקדש) also apply to ordinary slaughter (outside). The תנא קמא says no, so the gentile's thoughts do not ruin the שחיטה. רבי אליעזר says yes, so they can ruin it.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn / we derive (one law from another)
Outside: ordinary slaughter done outside the מקדש
Inside: slaughter of קדשים done in the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: 'Outside' and 'inside' here are not about rooms. 'Inside' means קדשים in the מקדש, and 'outside' means regular, non-holy slaughter.

phrases.english: we do not derive.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous עמוד: the תנא קמא does not learn outside from inside.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer comes to say:
we derive outside from inside,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the משנה's opinions that began on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא does not learn outside from inside. רבי אליעזר does, so a gentile's intent can make ordinary slaughter invalid.

steps.title: Explaining רבי יוסי: one person's thought does not ruin another's act
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that even inside the מקדש, one person's intent does not ruin the act of the person who actually slaughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי comes to say: even inside, we do not say 'this one thinks and that one performs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third opinion in the משנה, that of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי goes further than the תנא קמא. Even with קדשים inside the מקדש, the owner's bad thought does not ruin a שחיטה that someone else performs. So a gentile owner's thought surely cannot ruin a Jew's slaughter outside.

keyTerms.meaning: This one thinks and that one does: one person has the intent while another person does the act
We say / we apply (a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. The תנא קמא does not learn outside from inside. רבי אליעזר does. רבי יוסי holds that even inside, one person's thought does not affect another person's act.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei comes to say:
even inside, also,
"this one has intent and that one performs"
phrases.notes: He means the owner has the bad thought, but a different person does the slaughtering.

phrases.english: we do not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third opinion after the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with קדשים, the owner's intent does not invalidate a שחיטה that another person performs.

steps.title: New dispute: slaughtering in order to offer the blood or fat to עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute between אמוראים about someone who slaughters an animal planning to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one who slaughters an animal in order to sprinkle its blood for עבודה זרה, or to burn its fat for עבודה זרה: רבי יוחנן says it is פסולה, and רבי שמעון בן לקיש says it is מותרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a disagreement between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter itself was not for idols. The bad plan is only about a later act, sprinkling the blood or burning the fat. The question is whether a plan about that later act ruins the שחיטה being done now.

keyTerms.meaning: To sprinkle its blood
To burn its fat (on an altar)
Idol worship
Invalid: the slaughter does not work, and benefit is forbidden
Permitted

phrases.english: It was stated: one who slaughters the animal
to sprinkle its blood for idol worship,
or to burn its fat for idol worship –
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: it is not valid,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מוּתֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion that builds on the idea of learning outside from inside, from steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: פסולה. ריש לקיש: מותרת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן invalidates the animal for two reasons. A bad thought about a later עבודה counts, and we learn outside from inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it is פסולה because we carry intent over from one עבודה to another, and we learn outside from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two ideas behind רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, a bad plan about the blood or fat, held during the שחיטה, ruins the קרבן. Since רבי יוחנן learns outside from inside, the same is true for ordinary slaughter outside. That is why the animal is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: We carry intent from one service to another: a thought during one עבודה about a later עבודה counts

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says it is not valid:
one transfers intent from rite to rite,
phrases.notes: He means that while slaughtering, a thought about the later sprinkling or burning already counts.

phrases.english: and we derive outside from inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought about a later עבודה counts, and outside is learned from inside, so the animal is פסולה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש permits the animal. He holds that a bad thought about a later עבודה does not count, and that we do not learn outside from inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says it is מותרת because we do not carry intent over from one עבודה to another, and we do not learn outside from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two ideas behind ריש לקיש's ruling. They are the opposite of רבי יוחנן's two ideas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, a thought during the שחיטה about the blood or fat does not ruin even a קרבן. On top of that, rules of the מקדש do not carry over to ordinary slaughter. So the animal is מותרת.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not carry over intent
We learn (same meaning as יָלְפִינַן)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree on two separate ideas. Does a thought about a later עבודה count? Do we learn outside from inside? רבי יוחנן says yes to both, and ריש לקיש says no to both.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says it is permitted:
one does not transfer intent from rite to rite,
and we do not derive outside from inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reasoning to רבי יוחנן's in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought about a later עבודה does not count, and outside is not learned from inside, so the animal is מותרת.

steps.title: The same two sages argue about a second case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש stay consistent. They also argue about someone who slaughters a קרבן לשמה but plans to sprinkle its blood שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they each follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: if someone slaughtered a חטאת for its own sake, planning to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake, רבי יוחנן says it is unfit and רבי שמעון בן לקיש says it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. It shows that they argue here the same way they argued about the עבודה זרה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter itself was done properly, with the right intent. The only problem is a plan about a later step, the sprinkling of the blood. So the question again is whether a bad thought about a later עבודה ruins the current one.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning (they stay consistent)
For its own sake (for the right type of קרבן)
Not for its own sake (as if it were a different קרבן)
Invalid, unfit
Valid, fit

phrases.english: And they follow their reasoning, as it was stated:
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש from the last two steps.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it for its own sake
in order to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: it is unfit,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the argument in steps 4-5 matches another known argument between the same sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of slaughtering לשמה while planning to sprinkle the blood שלא לשמה, רבי יוחנן says פסולה and ריש לקיש says כשרה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason for invalidating
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a thought during one עבודה about another עבודה counts. He learns this from מחשבת פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it is unfit: we carry a thought over from one service to another, and we learn this from the thought of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן says the קרבן is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With פיגול, we already know that a thought during one עבודה about doing a later עבודה past its time ruins the קרבן. רבי יוחנן says the same works for a שלא לשמה thought. A bad plan during the slaughter about the sprinkling ruins the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A thought during one service about another service counts
We learn (one law from another)
The intent to do a service of the קרבן after its proper time, which ruins the קרבן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says it is unfit:
one's thought carries from one service to another service,
and we learn this from the intent of פיגול.
phrases.notes: פיגול is a plan to do part of the קרבן after its time. We know such a plan ruins the קרבן even when it is made during an earlier step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought about a later עבודה counts, learned from מחשבת פיגול, so the קרבן is פסולה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reason for permitting
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says a thought about a different עבודה does not count, and we do not learn from מחשבת פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says it is fit: a thought does not carry from one service to another, and we do not learn this from the thought of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש says the קרבן is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש agrees that פיגול works across different steps. But he says that is a special rule for פיגול alone. Other bad thoughts, like שלא לשמה, only count when they are about the step being done right now.

keyTerms.meaning: A thought during one service about another service does not count
We do not learn (from that source)
One of the steps of bringing a קרבן (slaughtering, sprinkling, burning)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר כְּשֵׁרָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says it is fit:
one's thought does not carry from one service to another service,
and we do not learn from the intent of פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives ריש לקיש's opposite reasoning, parallel to רבי יוחנן's reasoning in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought about a different עבודה does not count, and פיגול is not a model for other thoughts, so the קרבן is כשרה.

steps.title: Why we need the idol worship case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why both arguments were needed. From the עבודה זרה case alone, we might think ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן in the case of a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both were needed. If they had only argued about that case (עבודה זרה), we would say ריש לקיש permits there only because we do not learn outside from inside. But when learning inside from inside, he would agree with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not say out loud: why record two arguments that look the same? This step gives the first half of the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the עבודה זרה case, ריש לקיש had two reasons to permit. One of them was that ordinary slaughter outside the מקדש is not learned from קרבנות inside. In the case of a קרבן, that reason does not apply, so we might have thought he agrees there. The second argument teaches that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed (both statements are necessary)
Learning ordinary slaughter outside the מקדש from קרבנות inside
Learning one קרבן law from another קרבן law
He agrees

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the words בהא and בהך. In this step, בהא means the עבודה זרה case from step 3, not the case from step 6.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is explaining why we needed to hear their argument twice.

phrases.english: for if it had been stated only in this case,
phrases.notes: "This case" is the one about slaughtering for עבודה זרה, from step 3.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: we would say it is in this case that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says it is fit,
because we do not learn outside from inside,
but when learning inside from inside,
I would say he agrees with Rabbi Yoḥanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining why both the עבודה זרה argument and the שלא לשמה argument are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא (showing that both statements are needed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the עבודה זרה case alone, we might think ריש לקיש would agree with רבי יוחנן in the קרבן case, since there it is פנים מפנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קרבן case teaches that ריש לקיש permits even there.

steps.title: Why we need the sacrifice case too, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: From the קרבן case alone, we might think רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש in the עבודה זרה case. So both arguments are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had been stated only in that case (the קרבן), we would say רבי יוחנן invalidates only there. But in this case (עבודה זרה), he would agree with ריש לקיש. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the answer and ends with the conclusion that both arguments were needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the קרבן case, רבי יוחנן only needs to learn one קרבן law from another. In the עבודה זרה case, he would also need to learn חוץ מפנים, which is a bigger step. So we might have thought he permits there, and the עבודה זרה argument teaches that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (here: the קרבן case)
That case
I would say (we might have thought)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן invalidates in both cases: a bad thought about a later עבודה counts, and we learn חוץ מפנים. ריש לקיש permits in both cases. Each argument was needed so we would not think one sage agrees with the other in the other case.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only in that case,
phrases.notes: Here "that case" is the קרבן slaughtered with a plan to sprinkle its blood שלא לשמה.

phrases.english: we would say it is in that case that Rabbi Yoḥanan says it is unfit,
but in this case,
phrases.notes: This means the עבודה זרה case again.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: I would say he agrees with Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
therefore it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא that began in step 9 with its opposite side.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both arguments are needed. Without the עבודה זרה case, we might think רבי יוחנן agrees there. Without the קרבן case, we might think ריש לקיש agrees there.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes רבי יוסי's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת opens a challenge by quoting רבי יוסי's קל וחומר: if in קדשים everything follows the one doing the עבודה, then in חולין everything should follow the one slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raised an objection. רבי יוסי said: This is a קל וחומר. With holy animals, where a wrong thought can make the קרבן unfit, we only care about what the person doing the service is thinking. So with regular animals, where a thought does not make it unfit, surely we should only care about what the slaughterer is thinking!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת quotes רבי יוסי from the משנה to set up a challenge. The actual attack comes in the next steps, once the גמרא explains what רבי יוסי really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי argues from the stricter case to the more lenient one. In קדשים, where thoughts matter a lot, only the worker's thought counts. So in חולין, where thoughts matter less, surely only the slaughterer's thought counts, and the owner's (the נכרי's) thought does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one, or the other way around
A thought that makes the קרבן unfit
Holy animals set aside as קרבנות
Regular, non-holy animals
The one doing the service, usually the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not agreeing with רבי יוסי here. He is quoting him so he can use his words as a challenge against רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
Rabbi Yosei said:
The matter is a kal vachomer:
If in a place where thought disqualifies, with holy animals,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אֶלָּא אַחַר הָעוֹבֵד,
phrases.english: everything follows only the one doing the service,
then in a place where thought does not disqualify, with regular animals,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ
phrases.english: is it not logical that everything should follow
only the one who slaughters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue in both cases, the גמרא brings a challenge to both from רבי יוסי in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: רבי יוסי's words will be shown to contradict each of them in a different case.

steps.title: What does 'thought does not disqualify in חולין' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי means. It cannot mean thought never matters in חולין, because slaughtering for עבודה זרה does make an animal forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'thought does not disqualify with regular animals' mean? If you say thought never disqualifies at all, then how could there ever be a slaughter for עבודה זרה that makes the animal forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבי יוסי's phrase really means. It rules out the simple reading that thought never matters in חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know that if someone slaughters a regular animal for עבודה זרה, the animal becomes forbidden. So a thought clearly can matter in חולין. That means רבי יוסי must have meant something narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject)
Slaughtering an animal for עבודה זרה
It becomes forbidden
How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: What is meant by 'thought does not disqualify with regular animals'?
If you say it does not disqualify at all,
then a slaughter for idol worship that makes it forbidden,
how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a key phrase in רבי יוסי's קל וחומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what sense does thought 'not disqualify' in חולין?

steps.title: רבי יוסי means a thought about a different עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The phrase must mean that in חולין, a thought about a different עבודה does not count, only a thought about the same עבודה. In קדשים, it does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be about a thought from one עבודה to another. This is what רבי יוסי means: with holy animals, where a thought during one עבודה about another עבודה disqualifies, we still only care about the worker's thought. With regular animals, where a thought about a different עבודה does not count, only a thought about that same עבודה, surely we should only care about the slaughterer's thought!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question and rereads רבי יוסי's קל וחומר with the correct meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between קדשים and חולין is now about thoughts that jump to another עבודה. In קדשים such a thought counts. In חולין it does not; only a thought about the act being done right now counts. This reading sets up the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
From one עבודה to another: a thought during one act about a later act
In that same act
And this is what he is saying (a rereading of a statement)

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious it means from one service to another service,
and this is what he is saying:
If in a place where thought disqualifies with holy animals
from one service to another service,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אֶלָּא אַחַר הָעוֹבֵד,
phrases.english: everything follows only the one doing the service,
then in a place where thought does not disqualify with regular animals
from one service to another service,
but only within that same service,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ
phrases.english: is it not logical that everything should follow
only the one who slaughters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and rereads רבי יוסי accordingly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי means that in קדשים a thought from one עבודה to another counts, but in חולין only a thought within the same עבודה counts.

steps.title: רבי יוסי contradicts both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The קדשים half of רבי יוסי's words is a problem for ריש לקיש, and the חולין half is a problem for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case 'inside' (קדשים) is a difficulty for ריש לקיש, and the case 'outside' (חולין) is a difficulty for רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב ששת's challenge lands: each sage is contradicted by one half of רבי יוסי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said a thought about a different עבודה never counts, but רבי יוסי says it does count in קדשים. רבי יוחנן said such a thought counts even with עבודה זרה in חולין, but רבי יוסי says it does not count in חולין. So one source hits both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside: the קדשים case, done in the בית המקדש
Outside: the חולין case, done outside the בית המקדש
It is a difficulty

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, a thought about a different עבודה counts in קדשים but not in חולין. That splits the difference and challenges both רבי יוחנן (on חולין) and ריש לקיש (on קדשים).

phrases.aramaic: פְּנִים קַשְׁיָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Inside is difficult for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
phrases.notes: 'Inside' means the holy animals in the בית המקדש. רבי שמעון בן לקיש is ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: outside is difficult for Rabbi Yochanan!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּנִים קַשְׁיָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reading of רבי יוסי from step 13 against the positions in steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש (in קדשים) and רבי יוחנן (in חולין / עבודה זרה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי counts a thought about another עבודה in קדשים, against ריש לקיש, and does not count it in חולין, against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The inside half is fine for ריש לקיש, but the outside half hurts רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת narrows his challenge. The קדשים half can be explained for ריש לקיש, but the חולין half remains a real problem for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the 'inside' part is no problem for ריש לקיש: one statement of his was from before he heard it from רבי יוחנן, and the other was from after he heard it. But the 'outside' part is a problem for רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sorts out which half of רבי יוסי's words is a real problem. It says the problem for ריש לקיש goes away, but the problem for רבי יוחנן stays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים, רבי יוסי counts a thought about a different עבודה, which seems to go against ריש לקיש. But ריש לקיש said that only before he heard the משנה from his teacher רבי יוחנן, and afterward he agreed. For רבי יוחנן there is no such way out: רבי יוסי says that in חולין a thought about a different עבודה does not count, while רבי יוחנן holds that in an עבודה זרה case it does.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it works out well. This sets up a contrast: one side is fine, but the other is not.
Inside, meaning קדשים slaughtered in the Temple
Outside, meaning חולין slaughtered outside the Temple
Before / after

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ריש לקיש is simply contradicting himself. The גמרא is saying he changed his mind once he heard the משנה from רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Granted, the case of 'inside'

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: is not difficult for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
this was before he heard it from Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: 'This' is ריש לקיש's view that a thought does not carry over from one עבודה to another.

phrases.english: that was after he heard it from Rabbi Yochanan.
But 'outside' is difficult for Rabbi Yochanan!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא פְּנִים, לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the two-sided challenge of step 14. One side is resolved here, and the other side, against רבי יוחנן, is answered in the next step.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי says that in חולין a thought about a different עבודה does not count. רבי יוחנן says that in an עבודה זרה case it does count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial resolution for ריש לקיש: he changed his view after hearing it from רבי יוחנן

steps.title: רב ששת answers his own question: רבי יוסי is talking about the four services
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת resolves his own challenge. רבי יוסי's words are about a wrong thought during the ארבע עבודות, not about a thought moving from one עבודה to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raises the question and he answers it: it is talking about the four services.
steps.whatsHappening: The same רב ששת who asked the question now answers it. He says רבי יוסי was talking about something else entirely: the four services of a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only worked if רבי יוסי meant a thought about a different עבודה. רב ששת now says רבי יוסי meant a wrong thought during any one of the ארבע עבודות of a קרבן. Read this way, רבי יוסי has nothing to say about our argument, so רבי יוחנן is no longer contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection
Resolves / answers
The four blood services of a קרבן: שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה, זריקה

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes רבי יוסי's קל וחומר as a source against either רבי יוחנן or ריש לקיש in their argument.

phrases.english: He raises the objection
and he resolves it:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב ששת, who brought the challenge in step 11.

phrases.english: it is about the four services,

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן left standing in step 15 by changing how רבי יוסי is read.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי was talking about a thought from one עבודה to another, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי was talking about a wrong thought during the ארבע עבודות, which has nothing to do with our argument.

steps.title: Rereading רבי יוסי's קל וחומר: in קדשים, the one doing the service decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins rewording רבי יוסי's קל וחומר in light of the new reading. In קדשים, a thought during the ארבע עבודות goes only after the one doing the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what he is saying: if in a place where a thought disqualifies sacrificial animals during the four services, everything follows only the one doing the service...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to read רבי יוסי's words again, the new way. This is the first half of the קל וחומר, and the second half comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, a wrong thought during any of the four services can make the קרבן פסול. Even there, only the thought of the person doing the service matters, not the owner's thought. This is the 'stronger' case, and the קל וחומר will build from it to חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: A thought disqualifies the קרבן
Consecrated animals (קדשים)
The one doing the service

phrases.english: and this is what he is saying:
If in a place where a thought disqualifies
in sacrificial animals, during the four services,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אֶלָּא אַחַר הָעוֹבֵד,
phrases.english: everything follows only the one doing the service,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁמַּחְשָׁבָה פּוֹסֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the new reading from step 16 by rewording the first half of רבי יוסי's קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the source to fit the new reading
